演奏雷科雷科竹刮器時，以木棒沿竹或木製鋸齒筒身刮奏；金屬筒附彈簧者改用金屬棒，音: To play the reco-reco, scrape a wooden stick along the notched bamboo or wooden body; on the metal-bodied type with springs, use a metal stick instead, which is louder. Some models have a hole at the bottom; begin with an even scrape, then cover the hole with the palm to change the timbre. The basic order for this idiophone is: hold the body steady, scrape with the stick, control speed and force.

雷科雷科竹刮器屬體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs編號112.22，以刮: The reco-reco is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 112.22, sounding when its notched body is scraped. The source shows it used as a percussion instrument in Brazilian music, and it is also found in many Latin American countries, where it is called güiro, güira, guayo or guacharaca; in Brazil it can be used in samba and related styles. The metal-bodied version with springs is louder, and a hole at the bottom can be covered with the hand to change the timbre.
雷科雷科竹刮器屬體鳴樂器，傳統琴身以竹或木製成鋸齒狀圓柱體，使用木棒刮奏；另有金: The reco-reco is an idiophone. Its traditional body is a notched cylinder of bamboo or wood, scraped with a wooden stick; there is also a metal cylinder with springs, scraped with a metal stick and louder. Bodies of fibreglass also exist today, though wooden ones remain commonest. The source does not record a hole in the bottom of the soundbox or the materials of other parts.
雷科雷科竹刮器源自非洲，作為體鳴樂器，以刮奏發聲，在巴西音樂中使用，並傳入多個拉: The reco-reco comes from Africa; as an idiophone it sounds by scraping, is used in Brazilian music, and has spread to several Latin American countries under the names güiro, güira, guayo and guacharaca. The traditional form is a notched bamboo or wooden cylinder scraped with a wooden stick; later came a metal cylinder with springs, scraped with a metal stick and louder, some with a hole at the bottom that can be covered to change the timbre. Fibreglass instruments exist today, but wooden ones remain commonest, and it appears in samba and other Brazilian styles.
雷科雷科竹刮器發出清脆而富有穿透力的音色，具有明亮且帶有粗糙質感的特點。其音域處: The reco-reco has a crisp, penetrating timbre, bright with a rough texture. Its range is in the middle-high frequencies, moderate in volume but highly recognisable. The instrument resonates through a stick rubbing on bamboo or wooden notches; the sound has a clear grain and a strong sense of rhythm, like rain or a rustling. Against the sharpness of metal scrapers the reco-reco sounds warmer and more natural; against a tambourine its sound is clearer and more directional, without metallic ringing. This quality lets it build a groove in a Brazilian samba band, giving a steady, lively percussion layer.
雷科雷科竹刮器（Reco-reco）是源自非洲的刮奏體鳴樂器，Hornboste: The reco-reco is a scraped idiophone from Africa, Hornbostel–Sachs number 112.22. It is traditionally a bamboo or wooden cylinder with notched grooves, scraped with a wooden stick; there is also a metal cylinder with springs, played with a metal stick, louder, some with a hole at the bottom that can be covered to change the timbre. It is used in Brazilian music and appears in several Latin American countries, in styles such as samba.
